correctness.rationale: Definitions and one-based indexing are fixed. For each parity, the explicit Schaeffer–Shallit Theorem-8 sets have the claimed size and fit the theorem parameter interval at length 2^m. The new lower proof lists ceil(m/2)+1 pairwise disjoint factor intervals, proves the factor spelling appears exactly once from gaps between consecutive powers of two, and hence forces that many distinct attractor positions. Odd m=3 and even m=2 are checked explicitly. The provided standard-library checker independently tests forced unique factors and interval disjointness for m=2..14 and full factor-occurrence coverage for m=2..9, all passing. No finite enumeration is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Exact dyadic minimum is not a consequence of the known published upper-bound witnesses alone. Schaeffer–Shallit Theorem 8 explicitly notes a matching lower bound is missing; the present disjoint uniquely occurring-factor packing supplies it in both parities. Béal–Crochemore–Romana Table 2 reports sizes from a greedy algorithm and not the optimum. Cassaigne et al. study general asymptotics, not this equality. Closest search hits concern other automatic-word families or different invariants, not the exact same-object minimum. Historical priority remains a stated limitation.

value.rationale: The sharp minimum attractor profile on dyadic prefixes is the natural exact invariant behind compression-style positions for the canonical automatic characteristic word, and a genuine gap explicitly noted in Schaeffer–Shallit Section 6. The elementary parity-separated unique-factor packing produces an all-order exact answer, in contrast to the 2025/2026 experimental greedy profile. No extension to arbitrary prefix lengths or counting all minimizers is claimed.
